title: The Atari E.T. burial: what was really in the ground
description: Atari buried games in a New Mexico landfill in 1983. When diggers returned in 2014, they found a different story than the myth.

scenes.sub: what was really in the ground
scenes.say: In 1983, Atari dumped games in a New Mexico landfill. The legend says millions of E.T. cartridges. The truth is stranger.
Atari's own manager said only about seven hundred twenty eight thousand cartridges were buried, across many different games, not just one.
Diggers returned on April twenty sixth, 2014, for the documentary Atari: Game Over. They recovered about thirteen hundred cartridges.

scenes.caption: Alamogordo, New Mexico
scenes.say: The E.T. share is unknown. Designer Howard Scott Warshaw doubted millions were ever destroyed, and Atari made about five million copies, selling roughly one and a half million.
So the myth was bigger than the dump, and the truth is still a great story. Follow for more gaming history, myths busted.
